service_boundary: Represents hosted APIs invoked from NVIDIA's API Catalog, not self-hosted NIM containers, NVIDIA hardware, downloadable model artifacts, or cloud partners operating their own NIM endpoints.
regional_controls: The hosted catalog documentation does not present customer-selected inference regions; production residency controls differ for self-hosted and partner-hosted NIM deployments.
retention_controls: Hosted API use follows NVIDIA API trial and service terms; model-specific and preview conditions must be reviewed before production use.
routing: Customers invoke a selected hosted NIM endpoint; the catalog is not a general automatic multi-provider router.
customization: Portable NIM microservices can be deployed elsewhere, but that customer- or partner-hosted path is outside this hosted-service record.
strengths: A broad multimodal catalog exposes documented APIs backed by NVIDIA's inference stack.
The same NIM packaging concept supports later migration to controlled deployments.
tradeoffs: Catalog-hosted endpoints and self-hosted NIM are materially different service boundaries.
Hosted catalog access may be evaluation-oriented or subject to model-specific availability.

response_integrity.note: No signature, attestation, or equivalent mechanism for verifying that a response arrived unaltered from the model appears in the API reference or the security documentation.
response_integrity.scope: NVIDIA API Catalog documentation, for the NVIDIA API Catalog

upstream_disclosure.note: The API trial terms state what the operator collects and shares: "NVIDIA will collect the following data, without identifying specific users, to operate and improve the API Services and other products and services: ... (iv) User Content and Generated Content to improve NVIDIA products and services, including AI models. Your use of the API Services will be logged for security, fraud or abuse monitoring and shared with third party service providers for this purpose." Those third parties are not named.
upstream_disclosure.scope: NVIDIA API trial terms of service, for the NVIDIA API Catalog

credential_handling.note: The API offers no customer-supplied-key path: "The NIM API uses keys to authenticate requests to the NVIDIA GPU Cloud (NGC). Follow the steps below to generate a personal API key to authenticate API requests."
credential_handling.scope: NVIDIA API Catalog authentication page, for the NVIDIA API Catalog

cache_isolation.note: No prompt or prefix caching scope is documented for the hosted catalogue endpoints; the only cache-reuse documentation found concerns self-hosted NIM containers.
cache_isolation.scope: NVIDIA API Catalog documentation, for the NVIDIA API Catalog

vulnerability_disclosure.note: NVIDIA publishes a company-wide vulnerability reporting page ("If you need to report a security issue, please use the appropriate contact points outlined below") with a disclosure programme and the NVIDIA PSIRT mailbox; it does not name the API Catalog.
vulnerability_disclosure.scope: NVIDIA report-a-vulnerability page, for the NVIDIA API Catalog

independent_audit.note: The AI trust centre says only that "NVIDIA is committed to external validation of its security posture. Learn more about our compliance offerings." and its compliance list does not name the API Catalog, so it is recorded as undocumented for the named service.
independent_audit.scope: NVIDIA AI trust centre compliance page, read for the NVIDIA API Catalog
